analysis.title: GS Saboureault - Positioning Mondays Week 40 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: US Fundamental L/S net leverage fell for a third consecutive week to its lowest level since April 2025 ('Liberation Day'), near five-year lows in the 2nd percentile.

The non-fundamental bid is weakening: CTAs are slated to sell $18.5bn of global equities this week, with many trend signals close to threshold levels, and the buyback bid is affected by the earnings blackout window.
Europe remains a relative hideout: GS PB flows were risk-on for a 2nd consecutive week, with new longs outpacing short covers, and EPFR shows inflows to Western Europe dedicated equity mutual funds.

Sentiment is depressed (AAII bearish, GS Sentiment Indicator negative, CNN Fear & Greed in Fear). The desk says this, combined with cautious fundamental positioning, offers potential contrarian support into Q4.

GS PB global overall book gross leverage was unchanged at 308.0% (55th percentile, 1-year) and net leverage unchanged at 77.4% (29th percentile). Fundamental L/S gross fell 1.7 pts to 206.2% and net fell 2.1 pts to 53.0% (7th percentile).

Global equities were net bought (+0.7 SDs, 1-year), with long buys outpacing short sales 2.7 to 1. All major regions except EM Asia were net bought, led in dollar terms by Europe and North America. Macro Products were net bought at the fastest pace in 2 months, driven by short covers. Single Stocks were net sold for a 3rd straight week, driven by short sales.
Most net bought global sectors: Health Care, Utilities, Energy. Most net sold: Comm Svcs, Cons Disc, Info Tech.
Europe on the GS PB book is overweight vs MSCI World by 2.42% (up 0.81 ppts WoW), while North America is underweight at -17.24% (greater by 0.25 ppts).
CFTC data shows asset managers were small net sellers of S&P futures in the week ending September 29.

EPFR global equity funds took in +$16bn in the week to September 30 vs -$10bn the prior week. DM saw inflows despite continued US fund outflows, EM inflows were driven by China funds, and technology then utilities funds led sector inflows. Inflows to Korea and Taiwan funds have slowed in recent weeks.
Retail flows stayed supportive despite lower participation on the last day of the month/quarter.

GS estimates CTAs are long $67bn of global equities after selling about $6bn last week. Selling over the past month is about $73.5bn globally, while SPX and NDX saw net buying of about $5bn combined. This week's forecast is $18.5bn of net selling, up to $16.5bn of it in EMEA in the base case. Baseline forecasts could grow larger through the week barring an equity retracement.

The buyback desk saw subdued execution at 0.8x 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.8x 2024 YTD ADTV. About 93% of the S&P 500 is in blackout, rising to 94% by the end of the week. Execution is 89% 10b5-1 plans vs 11% OMR (from 82%/18%). YTD buyback authorizations are $1.27T, +11% vs 2025 YTD. The desk expects activity to stay at these levels for the next few weeks and authorized capital to reactivate once Q3 earnings begin mid-October.
North America IPO/additional issuance was $2.19bn on the week and $509.25bn YTD.

Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 206.2% (21st percentile 1-year) and net leverage is 53.0% (7th percentile 1-year).

tension_points.bull_case: Sentiment is consensually depressed (AAII bears 46.5%, Fear & Greed 38) and fundamental positioning is cautious (L/S net leverage in the 2nd percentile). The desk says this offers potential contrarian support into Q4. Buyback authorizations of $1.27T should reactivate after Q3 earnings begin.
tension_points.bear_case: Fundamental L/S players are still de-risking for a third week. CTAs are slated to sell $18.5bn with trend signals near thresholds, and the buyback bid is muted by blackout, so a breach could trigger larger systematic unwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Breach of CTA trend-signal thresholds, which would lead to larger systematic unwinds (barring an equity retracement, baseline flow forecasts grow through the week).
